us1_aid.topic: What US aid to Israel is, its weight in Israel's economy and defence spending 1985-2025, and what it frees up

claims.text: Book's arithmetic (US fiscal-year aid over Israeli calendar-year GDP, both current $): 12.7% (1985), 5.6% (1990), 2.9% (2000), 1.3% (2010), 1.0% (2019), 2.3% (2024, incl. supplemental), 0.6% (2025)

Melnick and Mealem (2009): defence expenditure fell 'from more than 20% of GDP in the mid-1980s' to 'less than 10% recently'; inflation 'of over 400%' before the 1985 plan; plan's success 'was supported by the U.S. grant in the amount of $1.5 billion (over a two-year period)'; US loans for defence acquisitions converted into grants

Even (INSS, 2010): total defence cost incl. additional costs 10% of GDP in 1993, 8.2% in 2000, 7.8% in 2005; 7.0% in 2009 (CBS model); 2010 defence budget 6.7% of GDP; under the 2007 MOU 74% of aid for procurement in the US, 26% convertible to shekels; 2010 aid about $2.775bn
